# Felix Akwasi Sarpong

## Building rigorous computational methods for real scientific problems.

I am a graduate student in the Department of Mathematics and Statistics at Georgia State University. My work sits at the intersection of statistical computing, machine learning, numerical methods, optimization, and data-driven scientific research.

## What I work on

::: {.card-grid}
::: {.feature-card}
### Statistical Computing
Reproducible statistical analysis, Bayesian computation, resampling, survival analysis, longitudinal models, and high-dimensional methods.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Scientific Computing
Numerical optimization, matrix computation, algorithms, simulation, and computational approaches to mathematical problems.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Machine Learning
Predictive modeling, regularization, pattern recognition, time-series learning, and computational methods for scientific data.
:::
:::

## Selected work

::: {.project-grid}
::: {.project-card}
<span class="project-kicker">RESEARCH</span>
### Reservoir Computing & Brain Connectivity
Research on directed networks and resting-state effective brain connectivity using state-space reconstruction and reservoir-computing causality.

[View research →](research.html)
:::

::: {.project-card}
<span class="project-kicker">STATISTICAL LEARNING</span>
### Large-Scale NYC Taxi Prediction
Elastic-net modeling for large-scale taxi-trip prediction, comparing ridge, lasso, and elastic-net approaches on real transportation data.

[View projects →](projects.html)
:::

::: {.project-card}
<span class="project-kicker">BIOSTATISTICS</span>
### Longitudinal Brain-Volume Analysis
Response-profile analysis of normalized whole-brain volume using longitudinal OASIS cohort data.

[View projects →](projects.html)
:::
:::
